name: LADEE
short_status: Impacted the lunar far side near Sundman V crater April 18, 2014 (04:30-05:22 UTC window); LROC located the sub-3 m crater in October 2014.
tagline: NASA · United States · Orbiter · 2013 · The robotic return Success
stats: record laser downlink from lunar orbit, more than six times faster than the best radio flown to the Moon
dust impacts counted by LDEX, revealing the Moon's permanent, lopsided dust cloud
launch mass of the first Modular Common Spacecraft Bus, built at NASA Ames
width of the impact crater LROC found on the rim of Sundman V

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 7 September 2013, 03:27 UTC (September 6, 11:27 p.m. EDT), Minotaur V from Pad 0B, Mid-Atlantic Regional Spaceport, Wallops Flight Facility, Virginia

facts.label: Firsts at launch
facts.value: First flight of the Minotaur V and the first deep-space mission launched from Wallops

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: 383 kg (844 lb) fully fueled at launch; mission cost approximately $280 million including spacecraft development, science instruments, launch services and mission operations

facts.label: Builder
facts.value: Designed, developed, built and tested at NASA Ames Research Center; first flight of the Modular Common Spacecraft Bus

facts.label: Payload
facts.value: Three science instruments (Neutral Mass Spectrometer, Ultraviolet-Visible Spectrometer, Lunar Dust Experiment) plus the LLCD laser-communications technology demonstration

facts.label: Lunar orbit insertion
facts.value: 6 October 2013, followed by burns on October 9 and 12 into a 235 x 250 km checkout orbit

facts.label: LLCD laser record
facts.value: 622 Mbps downlink and error-free 20 Mbps uplink between lunar orbit and White Sands, New Mexico, October 2013; terminal built by MIT Lincoln Laboratory

facts.label: Science orbit
facts.value: Equatorial orbit about 20 x 60 km above the surface, entered 20 November 2013

facts.label: Dust cloud result
facts.value: LDEX recorded more than 140,000 dust impacts over the mission, revealing a permanent, asymmetric dust cloud sustained by interplanetary particle impacts (Nature, 17 June 2015)

facts.label: Exosphere result
facts.value: The exosphere is mostly helium, argon and neon; LADEE confirmed neon's presence for the first time (announced 17 August 2015)

facts.label: Impact
facts.value: 18 April 2014, between 04:30 and 05:22 UTC (9:30-10:22 p.m. PDT April 17), on the lunar far side at about 3,600 mph, planned to avoid all historic landing sites

facts.label: Crater (found Oct 2014)
facts.value: Under 3 m across at 11.8494 N, 266.7507 E, on the eastern rim of Sundman V about 780 m from the crater rim, roughly 295 m north of the predicted point; measured impact speed 1,699 m/s

timeline: Launch at 03:27 UTC on the first Minotaur V from Pad 0B, Wallops Flight Facility
Lunar orbit insertion burn places LADEE in an initial elliptical lunar orbit with a 24-hour period
In the early morning hours, LLCD transmits from lunar orbit to Earth at a record 622 Mbps, more than six times faster than any radio system flown to the Moon
Enters the 20 x 60 km equatorial science orbit
Mar 2014
100-day primary science phase complete; NASA extends mission operations for a final stretch of ever-lower passes
Survives the total lunar eclipse, hours of darkness and cold beyond its design case
Planned impact on the far side near Sundman V, confirmed in the 04:30-05:22 UTC window, at about 3,600 mph
LROC team releases before-and-after images pinpointing the sub-3 m impact crater on Sundman V's eastern rim
Nature publishes the LDEX result: the Moon flies inside a permanent, asymmetric dust cloud
NASA announces LADEE's first-ever confirmation of neon in the lunar exosphere
Nature Geoscience study of LADEE mass-spectrometer data shows meteoroid streams releasing ancient water from the lunar soil
